title: Character registry (authority file), version 1
description: One entry per character, companion, voice, group or prop. The only place a canonical name is written. Every other file holds {{id}} tokens or is checked against it. Field reference: docs/3-reference/REGISTRY-FIELDS.md

visual_continuity.description: Path of a visual-continuity manifest, relative to this file. Its stories' scenes_file and continuity_file become surfaces.

skip_stories.description: Manifest stories whose files are not surfaces, each with the reason (a fixture, a placeholder cast).

root.description: scenes: the key holding the scene map (default scenes).

fields.description: scenes: label fields (default characters, props, speaker, marginAuthor, dialogue[].speaker). Values are ids, aliases or tokens; never substrings.

paths.description: names: dot paths with * and [] wildcards whose string values are labels.

split.description: Extra separators for compound labels (default &, +, and).

pattern.description: headings: a regex whose first group is the label (default ### headings up to the first parenthesis).

within.description: headings: only lines after this exact heading line, up to the next heading of the same level.

prose.description: scenes: scan every string of each scene for retired names (default true).

ignore.description: headings: exact heading labels that are not characters (a timeline, a table) and are skipped.

story_field.description: prose: the field of each entry under root whose value picks the story through `stories` (default: the entry's key).

stories.description: prose: map from a story_field value (or entry key) to a story id; an entry whose value is not mapped is skipped.

skip_keys.description: Keys whose strings are not scanned, besides every key starting with _ (notes and sources).

key.description: A key (dot path allowed) no entry of this surface may hold, because another file owns that field.

owner.description: The file (or builder) that owns the field; the builder reads it from there.

forbid_keys.description: A field lives once. Listing a key here makes the gate fail any entry of this surface that still carries its own copy.

field.description: A scene field whose value picks one vocabulary (time_of_day, season, location_id).

values.description: For each value of the field, the words that belong to it. A scene whose prose uses a word of another value fails.

fields.description: The prose fields to scan (default: every string of the scene outside skip_keys).

required.description: True when a scene without the field fails instead of being skipped.

exclusive_markers.description: Declared vocabularies that may not mix: a scene labelled morning may not describe lamplight. Nothing is hardcoded; the words are yours.

kind.description: person; companion (an animal or a named companion object); voice (a device or document that speaks); group (members listed); prop (a named object a scene lists by id and a prompt describes from this entry, never by matching its name in prose).

story.description: Home story id (a visual-continuity story id, or any label such as moment-packs or platform).

also_in.description: Other story ids this character may appear in; "*" means every story.

role.description: One line. The profile holds the rest.

aliases.description: Every other label a surface uses for this character. Exact strings.

retired.description: Forms that may never return. A label equal to one, or a scene string containing one, fails.

first_appearance.description: A scene slug in the home story.

ages.description: Stated age anchors by year; checked against born.

continuity_ids.description: Keys in the home story's continuity file characters block.

sources.description: Files that describe this character, relative to the registry; a #fragment may follow the path.

questions.description: Open questions about this character that block nothing. Each line says who raised it and when.

prose_only.description: True when this character is named only inside prose, never on a label field, so the check does not report a gap.

species.description: companion: a key of the registry's species map (required for every companion).

generic.description: True for a descriptive label standing in for an unnamed person (The therapist): a label on its surfaces, not hunted in other stories' prose.

full_name.description: The full form a {{id:full}} token renders when the canonical name is shorter.

additionalProperties.description: A string (formal: Samantha) rendered by {{id:<form>}}, or a contextual form { "by": "<field>", "values": { "<value>": "text", "default": "text" } } whose text is picked by the field of the unit being resolved (a scene's stage, story_day, time_of_day). No default and no matching value means the build fails instead of guessing.

forms.description: Named forms. A form here overrides the built-ins first, short, full, initial.

prompt_tokens.description: prop or companion: the look a prompt writer compiles from this entry, written once here.

negative_tokens.description: prop or companion: what a prompt must avoid for this object.

image.description: The reference image every later generation conditions on, relative to the registry.

embeddings.description: The embeddings file the choice was computed from.

anchor.description: The visual anchor chosen for this character after drift, recorded by scripts/anchor.mjs --write or by hand (policy manual).

records.description: Globs (relative to this file; ** and * as in gitignore) of dated history that is never rewritten: the worklog, transcripts, decision records, research, past prompt records, retired plans, test fixtures. Every other tracked text file is scanned for retired names and companion species mismatches.

species.description: Species a companion may have, each with the words that name it in prose (nouns only; never a word that is also a verb). A story's text may name only the species of companions allowed in that story.

known.description: Problems the gate reports as gaps instead of failures while another lane or the owner resolves them: the file, a substring of the problem line, who owns it, the task and the date.

token_sources.description: Files that write no character's name: they hold {{id}} tokens and a builder renders the names (scripts/render.mjs or your own). Scene files, cards and prose surfaces are token sources already; list the rest (pages, partials, manifests, run notes a builder reads) here, as a path or a glob.

skip_keys.description: Keys whose strings are not checked: a label the file defines, printed text of a physical object, a dated note.

ignore.description: Globs of files that may write names and are nobody's surface: a README's examples, tests, the scripts themselves.

strict.description: True turns an unclassified file that names a character into a failure instead of a gap.

coverage.description: Every tracked text file is a surface, a token source, a record, or ignored here. A file that is none of those and names a character is reported, so the gate can never be silent about a file.

policy.description: origin: the first generated image; terminal: the last; consensus: the image nearest the centroid of all embeddings; mode: the most frequent attribute combination (tags), nearest the centroid among those.

metric.description: Name of the embedding the file holds (arcface, clip, dinov2, aura, ...). Informational; vectors from two encoders are never mixed.

pass_threshold.description: Cosine similarity to the anchor below which an image is listed for regeneration.

prune_outliers_z.description: Drop images whose distance to the centroid is more than this many standard deviations before choosing.

max_regeneration_budget.description: How many regenerations you are willing to pay for; the report compares policies against it.

embeddings.description: Default embeddings file for scripts/anchor.mjs, relative to the registry.

drift_resolution.description: How a visual anchor is picked after a character has drifted (docs/2-how-to/HOW-TO-RESOLVE-CHARACTER-DRIFT.md). Registry-level defaults; an entry may override.
